item.content:encoded: The images that were used in this article are non-compliant with the SCP wiki's license (CC BY-SA 3.0) as the first image is from Craig Donner and is copyrighted to him, the second image is owned by Atlas Obscura user Kimrad, the third image could not be found under any source as cc-compliant (it's the artpiece Inversion by Dan Havel and Dean Ruck), the fourth image couldn't be sourced, and the fifth image comes from here with no indication it has been released under Creative Commons. Thus, the images have been removed.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
A lot of scientific iffiness here. It really pulled me out of my willing suspension, but it's a great concept. Honestly, a simpler and more elegant theory and what I see when I read it, is that it's acting as though it is going at relativistic speeds when it isn't actually doing so. An experiment with the time dilation inherent to the gravitational pull(which would be significant considering the relative size of the area of effect) would easily give you an idea of what normal speeds correlate to which relativistic speeds.

Going into the specificity of the higgs and uncollapsed singularities seems pretty jarring. Like most SCPs, we don't know why it does what it does, we can only measure the effects of it.

Then again, this has a high number of likes, so perhaps all the iffiness is worth it for the pictures.

Edit: And I would think any physicist worth his doctorate would be amazed and intrigued by the fact that light apparently passes through this thing normally when at rest.
